title: Sport Legislation Amendment (World Anti-Doping Code Implementation) Bill 2026
short_title: Sport Legislation Amendment (World Anti-Doping Code Implementation) Bill 2026
portfolio: Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would update Australia's anti-doping legislation to reflect the revised World Anti-Doping Code, including rules about sanctions, appeals and publication of violations.
Sport Integrity Australia would impose provisional suspensions and sanctions, while athletes could ask the National Sports Tribunal to review refusals of therapeutic use exemptions.
The substantive amendments would start on 1 January 2027 or 28 days after Royal Assent, whichever is later, alongside changes to sporting policies.
changes: The Australian Sports Drug Medical Advisory Committee's separate review membership would be removed.
An exception to compulsory publication would cover final findings that a person bore no fault or negligence.
The definition of athlete would lose its automatic six-month extension after a person last competed.
Sporting bodies would no longer be required parties to anti-doping disputes unrelated to therapeutic use exemptions.
summary.affected: Athletes, support persons, sporting organisations, Sport Integrity Australia and the National Sports Tribunal are affected.
